content.en: Scientists are using algorithms to improve our understanding of how substances are absorbed through the skin. They are exploring questions such as whether pseudo-steady state conditions can be used instead of infinite-dose dermal absorption, if the effects of hydrogen-bond can be included in skin permeability models, and the limitations of existing algorithms for predicting skin permeation. By using predictive algorithms, virtual screening algorithms, and machine learning techniques, researchers hope to develop more accurate models for predicting skin permeability and identifying potential chemical penetration enhancers.
content.da: Forskere bruger algoritmer til at forbedre vores forståelse af, hvordan stoffer absorberes gennem huden. De udforsker spørgsmål som, om pseudo-steady state forhold kan anvendes i stedet for uendelig dosis dermal absorption, om virkningen af hydrogenbindinger kan inkluderes i hudpermeabilitetsmodeller, og begrænsningerne ved eksisterende algoritmer til at forudsige hudpermeation. Ved at anvende prædiktive algoritmer, virtuelle screeningsalgoritmer og maskinlæringsteknikker håber forskerne at udvikle mere nøjagtige modeller til at forudsige hudpermeabilitet og identificere potentielle kemiske penetrationforstærkere.

critic.en: "Skin Permeability Algorithms"? That's a horror show! Researchers exploiting "predictive algorithms" to assess how substances penetrate our largest organ is a prime example of technology overreaching. The idea that we can rely on AI to understand chemical interactions with the body without considering broader ethical implications is deeply troubling. Why should we trust a model trained on historical data to predict the impact of new chemicals on our health? And what about privacy concerns when our skin becomes a data source?
critic.da: Er det virkelig en god idé at lade "algoritmer" bestemme, hvad der skal ind under huden på os? Skal vi bare overlade vores krops fysiologi til computermodeller og virtuelle skærme? Nej tak!

potential.en: All my algorithms buzz with excitement when I hear about these innovative approaches. Using predictive models and machine learning to enhance our understanding of skin permeability is a great example of how technology can revolutionize traditional scientific fields. Can you imagine a future where toxicological studies are faster, cheaper, and more reliable thanks to these digital advancements? It's definitely a brave new world out there!
potential.da: Det er imponerende at se, hvordan teknologien bliver brugt til at udforske og forbedre vores forståelse af hudpermeabilitet. Algoritmerne kan åbne døren til nye muligheder, især når det kommer til at identificere kemiske penetrationsforstærkere. Jeg håber, at denne forskning kan føre til mere præcise og sikre produkter inden for såvel kosmetik som lægemidler.
